pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Allow to use NRPA with connectable advertiser
pr_body:
When starting connectable advertising and when CONFIG_BT_PRIVACY
Kconfig option is disabled, the host uses the advertising address from
the identity. When identity is BT_ID_DEFAULT, the address is either
public or static random.

For Bluetooth mesh, in certain cases, it is required to advertise as
connnectable with either RPA or NRPA where the adverting addresss
is regenerated in certain conditions.

This commit adds a new option, BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_RANDOM, which makes the
advertiser set generate a new random address and use it when it starts
advertising a connectable event.

Fixes #60428

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: Allow to use NRPA with connectable scannable undirected events
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
When Proxy feature is supported by a mesh node, when a mesh node advertises Mesh Proxy Service with Node Identity or Network ID, the Bluetooth mesh specification version 1.0.1 (currently adopted) requires a mesh node to advertise connectable undirected advertising events (section 7.2.2.2.1).

In the new Bluetooth mesh specification version 1.1 (not adopted yet), the node shall advertise using connectable __and scannable__ undirected advertising events, and when advertising with _Private_ Node Identity or _Private_ Network Identity the mesh node shall advertise using either __RPA or NRPA__ (sections 7.2.2.2.4, 7.2.2.2.5). The specification mandates the node to regenerate the address used in AdvA field.

Currently, when `BT_PRIVACY` feature is disabled (which is the case for Zephyr Bluetooth mesh stack), when starting connectable advertisement, the static random address of the identity used by advertiser is used (mesh always uses `BT_ID_DEFAULT`):
- When updating adv params for connectable advs, static random address is restored:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea2aac6e5131bf916abd1e37334e94cc3481e1a8/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/adv_ext.c#L159C1-L159C1 - > bt_le_ext_adv_update_param -> le_ext_adv_param_set -> bt_id_set_adv_own_addr -> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea2aac6e5131bf916abd1e37334e94cc3481e1a8/subsys/bluetooth/host/id.c#L1776-L1787
- Starting connectable advs, static randomn address is used:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea2aac6e5131bf916abd1e37334e94cc3481e1a8/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/adv_ext.c#L179 -> bt_le_ext_adv_start -> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea2aac6e5131bf916abd1e37334e94cc3481e1a8/subsys/bluetooth/host/adv.c#L1632-L1636

This doesn't allow to qualify Zephyr Bluetooth mesh stack with 1.1 mesh specification.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow to use NRPA in connectable advs when `bt_le_ext_adv_start` is called (like for non-connectable adv), or add API to manually regenerate the address at any time by mesh.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
Link to Bluetooth mesh spec 1.1: https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/specs/mesh-protocol-1-1/

If this is the case, then what is the purpose of `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY`? 

You write `This option is the opposite to BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY` - If that is the case, then what is the difference between `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY` not being set, and `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_RANDOM` being set?

Yes, this looks strange. But changing the current behavior will require users to update their advertiser options to get back the old behavior and this I wanted to avoid. Or do you think it should be done this way?

Have we documented the behavior of not using `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY` in a way that needs changing? 

I agree that we should be wary of changing behavior, but in the cases where the behavior is not documented, it's IMO less harmful.

Can we simplify the semantics on this and make it have the same effect independent of what this kconfig is set to?

Otherwise we will have to call it `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_NRPA_EXCEPT_IF_BT_PRIVACY` :P /s.

It doesn't seem to be possible as the behavior with `BT_PRIVACY` in general is different. But as long as behavior is clarified in the description, the current naming should be fine.

This option is the opposite to `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY`. But, when `BT_PRIVACY` is disabled, the host for some reasons (which aren't clear to me) restores the identity address if the address is random, instead of regenerating the new random address. If the host didn't do this, this new option wouldn't be needed as I could get the current behavior with setting `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY` and keeping the identity address unchanged, and get the desired behavior with removing the `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY` option.

(I rephrased this description a bit, renamed the option and added params check for it when it 
 is set with `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_USE_IDENTITY`).
